# KNOT-SO-EASY - R. Cameron - DREAMER 11 pp.19-20 (PDF pages 21-22) - CHIP-8 + machine code 0080-03D5
# (printed 0080-0400; picture data 0080-00FF printed at the bottom of p.19)
# run C000 (FN 3). A rope (string of dots) is drawn on the left of the screen in a 4 x 4 block of
# 8x8 squares; after a short time the computer jumbles (and rotates) the squares. Re-assemble it.
# keys: type a square's co-ordinates, 1-4 across then 1-4 down: on the last digit that square and the
# square to the right of the single dot interchange positions. 5 rotates (clockwise) the square,
# 6 checks: the picture flashes off straight away if wrong, a tone is heard if it is correct.
# Squares start at 0080 0088 0090 0098 / 00A0 ... / 00E0 00E8 00F0 00F8 (change them for a new picture).
# Machine code called with 0MMM: 02F6 swap, 02BA rotate (+02A8), 035D compare picture with 0080-00FF + tone.
# Reading notes (no printing errors corrected): 03B9 is a faint 'C6' (LDAB #32 / JSR C2E1 tone), first read
# as 06 (TAP/PULA crashed the check); the 0285 '02A8' has an ink blot on the A (02A8 is a valid entry).
# Quirk kept: 0394 BEQ 21 lands on 03B7 (STAA 39,X = 00 into display 0139, harmless) instead of 03B9.
# After '6' the digit is shown at (35,7) and erased: with a correct picture it stays during the tone.
